content: In July 2006, the mission of the Paul G. Rogers Society for Global Health Research was established to support research aimed at combating diseases that disproportionately affect the world's poorest nations. These diseases include those impacting child and maternal health, chronic conditions such as heart disease, diabetes, and tobacco-related illnesses, as well as HIV/AIDS, infantile diarrhea, intestinal parasites, neglected tropical diseases (e.g., hookworm, lymphatic filariasis, sleeping sickness, river blindness, and trachoma), malaria, malnutrition, obesity, and under-nutrition. Paul G. Rogers, a former U.S. Congressman from Florida who served from 1955 to 1979 and chaired the House Subcommittee on Health and the Environment from 1971 to 1979, was honored as Chair Emeritus for his contributions to healthcare policy and advocacy. In November 2006, the inaugural class of 27 Ambassadors for the Paul G. Rogers Society for Global Health Research was selected. These Ambassadors, all experts in global health research, were tasked with serving as representatives of the Society through June 2007. Among the notable members were: Dr. C. Ross Anthony, Director of Global Health at RAND. Dr. Margaret E. Bentley, Associate Dean for Global Health at UNC Chapel Hill. Dr. Eric G. Bing, a psychiatrist at Charles R. Drew University. Dr. Robert Edward Black, Chair of International Health at Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health. Dr. Michael Cappello, a professor at Yale University specializing in pediatrics, microbial pathogenesis, and public health. Dr. Lois K. Cohen, a consultant for the National Institute of Dental and Craniofacial Research. Dr. Christopher J. Elias, President of PATH. Dr. William B. Greenough III, a geriatrics professor at Johns Hopkins University. Dr. Richard L. Guerrant, Director of the Center for Global Health at the University of Virginia. Dr. Scott M. Hammer, Chief of Infectious Diseases at Columbia University. Dr. James E.K. Hildreth, Director of the Comprehensive Center for Health Disparities Research in HIV at Meharry Medical College. Dr. King Holmes, Chair of Global Health at the University of Washington. Dr. William Holzemer, Director of the WHO Collaborating Center at UCSF. Dr. Peter J. Hotez, Founding Dean of the National School of Tropical Health at Baylor College of Medicine. Dr. Michael Katz, Senior Vice President for Research at the March of Dimes Foundation. Dr. Jeffrey P. Koplan, Vice President for Academic Health Affairs at Emory University. Dr. Beverly McElmurry, Director of the WHO Collaborating Centre at the University of Illinois at Chicago. Dr. Marjorie Muecke, Assistant Dean for Global Health Programs at the University of Pennsylvania. Dr. Christopher J.L. Murray, Director of the Global Health Initiative at Harvard University. Dr. Gilbert S. Omenn, a professor at the University of Michigan. Dr. Nilda P. Peragallo, Dean of the School of Nursing at the University of Miami. Dr. Les Roberts, a public health expert at Columbia University. Dr. Thomas G. Streit, a professor at the University of Notre Dame. Dr. Sten H. Vermund, Chair in Global Health at Vanderbilt University. Dr. Kenneth E. Warner, Dean of Public Health at the University of Michigan. Dr. Peter F. Wright, Chief of Pediatric Infectious Diseases at Vanderbilt University. The Society's Advisory Council, established in 2006, was responsible for selecting Ambassadors from a pool of peer-nominated global health experts. The Council included distinguished members such as Nobel laureates and leaders in medicine, public health, and policy, including Dr. David Baltimore, Dr. Joseph Goldstein, and Dr. Leland Hartwell, as well as prominent figures like Sandra Day O'Connor and Bob Michel. The Paul G. Rogers Society received a grant from the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation to support its establishment and provide leadership development for its members. The organization facilitates public outreach and advocacy by engaging Ambassadors in meetings, speaking engagements, and community-level activities to connect with policymakers, opinion leaders, the media, and the public across the nation.
